katie: CI red for PR #954 — docusaurus build failed and the linkcheck flagged an internal anchor breaking: /docs/reference/architecture#runtime-flow. Also saw an MDX parse error about an unclosed HTML comment. Anyone touching SVGs or the mdx examples in this PR? docs-ci-bot: build failed: docusaurus build exit code 1 log excerpt: "Error: MDX parse error: Unexpected end of file (likely unclosed HTML comment) at docs/reference/architecture.md:42" linkcheck: Broken internal anchor: /docs/reference/architecture#runtime-flow -> 404 (target anchor not found) eli: I pulled the branch. The MDX problem is an HTML comment that spans a JSX block. Example from the file: ```mdx
` was accidentally removed in a squash. naveen: good catch. quick fix is to close the comment or convert it to a JS comment inside the JSX: `{/* NOTE: diagram below */}`. I'll patch that. zoe: about the missing anchor: the page references `#runtime-flow` which used to be provided by the embedded SVG title (`Runtime flow`) used as a fragment target by our old tooling. Docusaurus/HTML sanitizer strips `` out of inlined SVGs for security, so the anchor disappears on build. The static SVG file on the branch also had its `<title>` removed during an SVG optimization step. rachel: saw the same with another PR last month. Two pragmatic options: - Add an explicit heading `## Runtime flow` in the doc so the anchor is generated by the markdown parser (stable). - Or add an explicit id on the surrounding element: `<div id="runtime-flow">` before the SVG so the anchor exists even if the SVG loses its title. I prefer the explicit id on the containing element for now since the visual heading is undesirable in that spot. katie: both approaches sound reasonable. which is quicker for the hotfix? naveen: I'll do the minimal changes: (1) fix the MDX comment to not be an HTML comment, (2) add `<div id="runtime-flow">` wrapping the embedded svg/ExampleDiagram component so the anchor exists, and (3) restore the `<title>` in the source SVG files that we control (avoid stripping during optimization). Commit message: "docs(architecture): fix mdx comment and restore runtime-flow anchor". eli: can we also add a short postbuild check in the docs CI that verifies internal anchors referenced in markdown files actually exist in the built HTML? A fast static grep + simple HTML parse that checks `href` hashes against `id` attributes would catch this class of errors before linkcheck runs. zoe: yes — a lightweight `scripts/docs/anchor-smoke.js` that runs on PRs touching `docs/**` would be fast. We already have the linkcheck job but it runs after build and can be noisy; early static verification will be helpful. rachel: also suggest we change SVG optimizer config (svgo) to keep `<title>` and `aria-labelledby` for files under `docs/static/assets/diagrams`. That prevents accidental removal. katie: agreed. can we get the hotfix committed so I can re-run the preview? If the CI goes green we can then follow up with the svgo rule and the anchor-smoke job. docs-ci-bot: CI: rebuild triggered for PR #954 (branch: fix/mdx-comment-runtime-anchor) docs-ci-bot: build succeeded, preview deployed -> https://deploy-preview-954.docs.redwood.com/reference/architecture#runtime-flow eli: preview looks good. anchor resolves and no MDX parse errors. naveen: opened follow-up issue #418 to: (1) update svgo config to preserve titles/aria labels for docs svgs, (2) add `scripts/docs/anchor-smoke.js` to GH Actions on docs PRs, and (3) add a short note in CONTRIBUTING about preferring explicit `id` wrappers for inline diagrams if authors want stable anchors. katie: checklist before closing this thread: - [x] fix MDX comment and wrap diagram with `id="runtime-flow"` (naveen) - [x] restore title tags in source SVGs (naveen) - [ ] rachel: PR to update svgo exceptions for docs/* diagrams - [ ] zoe: add anchor-smoke GH Action (dry-run first) - [ ] eli: add CONTRIBUTING paragraph about stable anchors for diagrams katie: thanks everyone — merging the hotfix now. :tada:
